title: SSO via IdentityPort — per-customer IdP is the target shape; stub adapter for tests
context: P0-05 of the roadmap: enterprise buyers (banks, treasuries) expect SSO on the first call and won't accept a password-only app in a security review. The connector substrate (ADR-0004 / Phase 2 Stage 1) already defines IdentityPort with start_login/complete_login signatures and an IdentityAssertion dataclass, but there's no non-password adapter today and no customer picked. We want the code ready so when customer #1 names an IdP it's a new adapter file, not a cross-cutting refactor.
decision: SSO flows exclusively through IdentityPort. Each enterprise customer brings their own IdP (Entra, Okta, Google Workspace, Auth0) and we write one adapter per IdP family that implements the port. A StubOIDCIdentity adapter exists for tests and local dev — bindable via IDENTITY_PROVIDER=oidc_stub, in-process, no network — so SSO-shaped tests can be written and run today without a real provider. Default IDENTITY_PROVIDER stays local_password; no caller sees a difference until a real customer binds a real adapter.
scope_in: IdentityPort gains a mfa_passed field on IdentityAssertion so an IdP's own MFA claim surfaces to callers without changing method signatures.

StubOIDCIdentity adapter (backend/app/connector/adapters/identity/oidc_stub.py) with a test-only issue_code() helper that primes a profile; start_login/complete_login validate state + consume code exactly once (mirrors a real OIDC adapter's CSRF semantics).

role_mapper service (backend/app/services/role_mapper.py) reads sso_group_map (per-tenant table shipped in Phase 2 Stage 2) and returns the role set for a list of IdP groups. Fail-closed: no mapping = no role.
Registry factory in backend/app/connector/registry.py learns the oidc_stub branch; refuses unknown IDENTITY_PROVIDER values.
scope_out_deferred: A real OIDC adapter (EntraOIDCIdentity, Auth0OIDCIdentity, etc.) — writes when customer #1 names their IdP.
/auth/sso/start and /auth/sso/callback endpoints — the port is ready; the API surface comes with the first real adapter.
SAML. OIDC is the primary target; SAML goes in only if a customer insists.
JIT user provisioning on first SSO login — comes with the first real adapter.
SSO group-mapping admin UI — tracked under PHASE_2_ADMIN_UI_PLAN.md (parked).
Changing LocalPasswordIdentity. It stays as the default path; SSO is additive.
invariants: The default IDENTITY_PROVIDER is local_password. A deployment that doesn't set the env var behaves exactly as the pre-SSO code did.
role_mapper fails closed. An SSO caller whose group has no mapping gets zero roles — not a default role.
StubOIDCIdentity is for tests and dev. A deployment with IDENTITY_PROVIDER=oidc_stub in prod is a configuration error; nothing in the stub reaches a real IdP.
The port interface is additive-only going forward. New fields on IdentityAssertion get safe defaults so old adapters keep working.
consequences: backend/app/connector/ports.py — IdentityAssertion.mfa_passed field added with default False.
backend/tests/test_identity_sso_shape.py — 15 tests covering port shape, stub round-trip, registry wiring, role mapper (empty / mapped / case / per-tenant / empty-input).
No existing endpoint behaviour changes. Full regression stays green.
